knowledge_point.title: Determining the Equation of a Normal Line to a Curve at a Point

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=x^3+x+1$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=3x^2+1.
$$

At $(1,3)$ the tangent slope is $f'(1)=4$, so the normal slope is $-\frac{1}{4}$. Use point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-3&=-\frac{1}{4}(x-1)\\
4y-12&=-x+1\\
x+4y&=13.
\end{aligned}
$$

The first blank is $4$ and the second is $13$.

knowledge_point.title: Determining the Equation of a Normal Line to a Curve at a Point

question.:question/worked-solution:
The tangent slope is

$$
f'(1)=2(1)=2.
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so its slope is

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Use the point $(1,1)$ in point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-1&=-\frac{1}{2}(x-1)\\
y&=-\frac{1}{2}x+\frac{3}{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The first blank is $-\frac{1}{2}$ and the second is $\frac{3}{2}$.

knowledge_point.title: Determining the Equation of a Normal Line to a Curve at a Point

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=- \frac{x^{6}}{8} + x^{3} - 1$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=- \frac{3 x^{5}}{4} + 3 x^{2}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(2\right)=- \frac{3 \left(2\right)^{5}}{4} + 3 \left(2\right)^{2}=-12
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(-12\right)}=\frac{1}{12}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-1\right)&=\frac{1}{12}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{12}+\left(- \frac{1}{6}\right)+\left(-1\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{12} - \frac{7}{6}\\
\left(-12\right)y&=-x+\left(2\right)+\left(12\right)\\
x+\left(-12\right)y&=14
\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient is $-12$ and the constant is $14$.

knowledge_point.title: Determining the Equation of a Normal Line to a Curve at a Point

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=- x^{2} + x$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=1 - 2 x
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(2\right)=1 - 2 \left(2\right)=-3
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(-3\right)}=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-2\right)&=\frac{1}{3}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{3}+\left(- \frac{2}{3}\right)+\left(-2\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{3} - \frac{8}{3}\\
\left(-3\right)y&=-x+\left(2\right)+\left(6\right)\\
x+\left(-3\right)y&=8
\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient is $-3$ and the constant is $8$.

knowledge_point.title: Determining the Equation of a Normal Line to a Curve at a Point

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=- 2 x^{3} + x + 2$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=1 - 6 x^{2}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(1\right)=1 - 6 \left(1\right)^{2}=-5
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(-5\right)}=\frac{1}{5}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(1\right)&=\frac{1}{5}\left(x-\left(1\right)\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{5}+\left(- \frac{1}{5}\right)+\left(1\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{5} + \frac{4}{5}\\
\left(-5\right)y&=-x+\left(1\right)+\left(-5\right)\\
x+\left(-5\right)y&=-4
\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient is $-5$ and the constant is $-4$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=- 2 x^{2} + x + 2$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=1 - 4 x
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(-1\right)=1 - 4 \left(-1\right)=5
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(5\right)}=- \frac{1}{5}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-1\right)&=- \frac{1}{5}\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right)\\
y&=- \frac{x}{5}+\left(- \frac{1}{5}\right)+\left(-1\right)\\
y&=- \frac{x}{5} - \frac{6}{5}\\
\left(5\right)y&=-x+\left(-1\right)+\left(-5\right)\\
x+\left(5\right)y&=-6
\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient is $5$ and the constant is $-6$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{x^{6}}{8} - x^{3} - 2$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=\frac{3 x^{5}}{4} - 3 x^{2}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(2\right)=\frac{3 \left(2\right)^{5}}{4} - 3 \left(2\right)^{2}=12
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(12\right)}=- \frac{1}{12}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-2\right)&=- \frac{1}{12}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)\\
y&=- \frac{x}{12}+\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)+\left(-2\right)\\
y&=- \frac{x}{12} - \frac{11}{6}\\
\left(12\right)y&=-x+\left(2\right)+\left(-24\right)\\
x+\left(12\right)y&=-22
\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient is $12$ and the constant is $-22$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2 x^{2} - x - 1$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=4 x - 1
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(1\right)=4 \left(1\right) - 1=3
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(3\right)}=- \frac{1}{3}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(0\right)&=- \frac{1}{3}\left(x-\left(1\right)\right)\\
y&=- \frac{x}{3}+\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)+\left(0\right)\\
y&=\frac{1}{3} - \frac{x}{3}
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $a=- \frac{1}{3}$ and $b=\frac{1}{3}$.

$$
f'(x)=- 4 x - 1
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(-1\right)=- 4 \left(-1\right) - 1=3
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(3\right)}=- \frac{1}{3}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-3\right)&=- \frac{1}{3}\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right)\\

y&=- \frac{x}{3} - \frac{10}{3}

$$

Thus $a=- \frac{1}{3}$ and $b=- \frac{10}{3}$.

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=x^{2} - 1$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=2 x
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(-1\right)=2 \left(-1\right)=-2
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(-2\right)}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(0\right)&=\frac{1}{2}\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2}+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+\left(0\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2} + \frac{1}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $a=\frac{1}{2}$ and $b=\frac{1}{2}$.

knowledge_point.title: Determining the Equation of a Normal Line to a Curve at a Point

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2 x^{2} + 2 x + 2$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=4 x + 2
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(-1\right)=4 \left(-1\right) + 2=-2
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(-2\right)}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(2\right)&=\frac{1}{2}\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2}+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+\left(2\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2} + \frac{5}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $a=\frac{1}{2}$ and $b=\frac{5}{2}$.
